subject.title: [Bug] v2026.5.22 启动后 Gateway CPU 持续 100%+，导致请求延迟飙升 50-100 倍

question: Should normal gateway startup keep eager provider-auth prewarming by default, or should startup warming become explicit opt-in while retaining auth-profile failure rewarm?
rationale: Current main mitigates the event-loop impact by using a worker, but the remaining default behavior is still a provider/auth startup contract choice with upgrade impact.

options.title: Accept Lazy Startup Auth
options.body: Refresh and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88514 so default startup skips unsolicited provider-auth warm work while explicit opt-in and failure-triggered rewarm stay covered.

options.title: Keep Eager Startup Warm
options.body: Leave current main behavior in place and close or redirect the default-off PR if maintainers prefer first-call/provider-auth readiness over removing startup CPU work.

options.title: Require More Live Proof
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until maintainers get upgrade/live-provider proof showing default-off startup warming does not regress auth readiness.

recommendation.title: Accept Lazy Startup Auth
recommendation.body: Refresh and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88514 so default startup skips unsolicited provider-auth warm work while explicit opt-in and failure-triggered rewarm stay covered.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the current open maintainer PR changing this exact startup default.
